issue_context.title: Duplicate Entries From History Call
issue_context.body:
<!--- This template provides sections for bugs and features. Please delete any irrelevant sections before submitting -->

#### Expected Behavior
When requesting historical data, each row in the resulting DataFrame should be unique.
<!--- Required. Describe the behavior you expect to see for your case. -->

#### Actual Behavior
When requesting history with
```
qb = QuantBook()
symbols = [ Symbol.Create(x, SecurityType.Forex, Market.Oanda) 
            for x in ["EURUSD","GBPUSD","USDCAD", "AUDUSD", "NZDUSD"] ]
qb.History(symbols, datetime(2010, 11, 5), datetime(2010, 11, 8), Resolution.Daily)
```
the resulting DataFrame contains duplicate entries, as seen below:

> EURUSD 8G  2011-11-03 20:00:00    1.382260
>            2011-11-04 20:00:00    1.378930
>            2011-11-04 20:00:00    1.378930
>            2011-11-06 20:00:00    1.378800

<!--- Required. Describe the actual behavior for your case. -->

#### Potential Solution
Unknown.
<!--- Optional. Describe any potential solutions and/or thoughts as to what may be causing the difference between expected and actual behavior. -->

#### Reproducing the Problem
See the backtest and notebook [here](https://www.quantconnect.com/terminal/processCache?request=embedded_backtest_0b1ebfd55ae4878b16209770daf7dced.html).
<!--- Required for Bugs. Describe how to reproduce the problem. This can be via a failing unit test or a simplified algorithm that reliably demonstrates this issue.  -->

#### System Information
Run in the QC web terminal. Windows 10.

review_comments: nit - XML docs seem outdated, would be nice to explain and reference the issue being tested
Nice regression test 👍  thanks for getting it to run locally

Changes in this method are high risk and hard to understand 😅 , I believe we need more code comments about what's happening here for example: why `_offsetProvider.ConvertFromUtc(previousTimeUtc)` and not directly `previous.Time`? Why can't we use `next.EndTime` directly? Why `previous.Time + nextPreviousTimeDelta` instead of `previous.EndTime`? Else we will forget and change it back. Think we need simple unit tests covering these `why` too.

Just a note: `potentialBarEndTime` in the other hand isn't affected by the daylight savings since it's generated from UTC after fixing a similar issue that caused an infinite loop situation see https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/issues/3707, and before this change `next.EndTime` was affected and it caused this issue
exactly. potentialBarEndTime is calculated using right _offsetProvider movement and didn't swallow hour anywhere
